s1.syndrome_frame: Acute vision loss in one eye with optic disc swelling and retinal vascular occlusion in a patient undergoing immunotherapy
salient_findings: Sudden vision loss in the right eye
Marked swelling of the optic disc
Peripapillary retinal hemorrhages and occlusion of the superior branch artery
Combined occlusion of the central retinal artery and vein
key_facts: Patient is a woman in her 40s
Undergoing treatment with systemic steroids, durvalumab, and bevacizumab
Initial visual acuity of 20/25 OU
Right eye showed full visual field and relative afferent pupillary defect
Mild swelling of the optic disc on initial examination
Vision loss occurred 10 days after initial presentation
MRI showed focal enhancement along enlarged right optic nerve
Lumbar puncture showed no abnormalities
Vitreous biopsy showed hypercellular sample with astrocytic neoplasm
Immunohistochemistry positive for glial fibrillary acid protein and mutant IDH-1 protein

salient_findings: Sudden vision loss in the right eye
Marked swelling of the optic disc
Peripapillary retinal hemorrhages and occlusion of the superior branch artery
Combined occlusion of the central retinal artery and vein

Undergoing treatment with systemic steroids, durvalumab, and bevacizumab
Initial visual acuity of 20/25 OU
Right eye showed full visual field and relative afferent pupillary defect
Mild swelling of the optic disc on initial examination
Vision loss occurred 10 days after initial presentation
MRI showed focal enhancement along enlarged right optic nerve
Lumbar puncture showed no abnormalities

Immunohistochemistry positive for glial fibrillary acid protein and mutant IDH-1 protein

differentials: Primary Angiitis of the Central Nervous System
Primary Angiitis of the Central Nervous System

shortlist.label: Central Retinal Artery Occlusion
shortlist.why_kept: Patient presented with sudden vision loss and retinal vascular occlusion

shortlist.label: Central Retinal Vein Occlusion
shortlist.why_kept: Combined occlusion of central retinal artery and vein was observed

shortlist.label: Ischemic Optic Neuropathy
shortlist.why_kept: Mild swelling of the optic disc on initial examination and subsequent vision loss

shortlist.label: Giant Cell Arteritis
shortlist.why_kept: Optic disc swelling and vision loss in one eye, although less likely given patient's age and lack of other symptoms

shortlist.label: Lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Vitreous biopsy showed hypercellular sample with astrocytic neoplasm, and patient is undergoing immunotherapy

raw.rationale: The patient's sudden vision loss, relative afferent pupillary defect, and optic disc swelling are more consistent with ischemic optic neuropathy. The presence of peripapillary retinal hemorrhages and occlusion of the superior branch artery also supports this diagnosis.
raw.anchor_refutation: Giant Cell Arteritis is unlikely due to the lack of systemic symptoms such as headache, jaw claudication, and polymyalgia rheumatica, as well as the absence of elevated inflammatory markers. The patient's age and treatment with systemic steroids, durvalumab, and bevacizumab do not strongly support Giant Cell Arteritis.

rejected.label: Giant Cell Arteritis
rejected.why: Lack of systemic symptoms and inflammatory markers

rejected.label: Central Retinal Artery Occlusion
rejected.why: While the patient developed central retinal artery occlusion, it was a secondary event following ischemic optic neuropathy

rejected.label: Central Retinal Vein Occlusion
rejected.why: The patient's presentation and imaging studies do not support central retinal vein occlusion as the primary diagnosis

rejected.label: Lymphoma
rejected.why: The vitreous biopsy showed an astrocytic neoplasm, which is not consistent with lymphoma
